extracted.intended_audience: filmmakers, entertainment-industry readers, and fans interested in film production and political satire
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for producing an ambush-comedy feature that functions as political satire (using hidden-camera encounters, disguises, improvisation, and narrative devices to expose subjects). Focuses on secrecy, casting, safety, timing, and balancing satire with comedic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of development and script
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the project cloaked in secrecy using methods such as encrypted expiring links, misleading character names, and deliberate obfuscation so the true nature of the film isn't discovered during development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team used an encrypted link that would expire in hours and repeatedly changed character nationalities (e.g., Guatemalan, Bulgarian, Moldovan) and even relied on typos as a kind of 'unbreakable code' — though collaborators noted it was an imperfect system ('Anyone within three minutes would figure it out').

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and strategic release
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan release timing to maximize political and cultural impact (e.g., schedule the film to open ahead of a critical political event or election).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baron Cohen wanted the film to open just ahead of the 2020 presidential election to ensure the film's political message had timely relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear political intent/purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the film's political purpose explicitly — the satire should serve an articulated aim (here described as 'peaceful protest' against a political movement or figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baron Cohen framed the film as 'a form of peaceful protest' intended to reveal what Trump supporters would tolerate and to confront the poisoning/division he perceived in American democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary creative objective: prioritize comedic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: While carrying political intent, the primary production aim should remain making the funniest movie possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baron Cohen: 'The first movie was a satirical comment... but [our job] was to make the funniest movie possible.' The film balances satire with comedy as the chief creative metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character choice as tactical device
rubrics_metrics.description: Design or select characters (e.g., Tutar, a young daughter) that can both drive the plot and function tactically in ambush interactions (not easily recognized, able to interact with subjects), while providing emotional stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tutar was selected because she could interact with interview subjects without recognition, drive the plot (gift to Mike Pence), and supply the film's emotional journey — the father-daughter relationship became integral once Bakalova's performance emerged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting: seek improvisational fearlessness and chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Cast performers who can improvise under pressure, use fear productively, and demonstrate strong chemistry with the lead; prioritize authentic, spontaneous responses over trained polish when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thousands auditioned; Maria Bakalova impressed by improvising in self-tapes and displaying chemistry with Baron Cohen. Directors praised her 'fearlessness' and ability to 'do it all.' Baron Cohen told her to 'use that fear' in confrontational scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of improvisation and adaptable scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain flexible, frequently changing scripts that allow room for improvisation and real-time adjustments to encounters with nonactors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early drafts constantly changed to maintain secrecy; the production embraced improvisation in auditions and on-set interactions to capture spontaneous reactions from nonactors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, legal, and logistical risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate physical danger, police involvement, and legal exposure when ambushing nonactors; have plans for crew safety and rapid exits, and accept that 'people will just call the cops when they’re confused.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production reported occasional threats of physical danger and frequent running from police; the crew had to be prepared to flee and manage unpredictable legal/logistical consequences of ambush filming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate current events and real-world constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When external events (e.g., a pandemic) affect production, adapt the story to incorporate those realities and consult relevant experts to maintain authenticity and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Half the film was shot before COVID halted production; writers incorporated the COVID-19 crisis into the plot and producers consulted epidemiologists and ER doctors to safely resume filming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and evidentiary aim: reveal tolerant behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hidden-camera encounters and satire to reveal what people are willing to tolerate or endorse, especially regarding racism, misogyny, and other social harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baron Cohen's stated aim was to force those who follow Trump to 'reveal what they were ready to tolerate,' using comedy as a tool to expose societal attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative heart and emotional stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor the satire with an emotional through-line (e.g., a father-daughter relationship) to humanize the story and raise audience investment beyond the ambush set pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers discovered Maria Bakalova's capacity for emotional work, which made the father-daughter relationship more integral and provided the film with a genuine emotional arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveraging high-impact scenes for cultural/political effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to create scenes that can influence public perception or discourse (e.g., a widely discussed ambush that discredits a public figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rudy Giuliani scene became a cultural moment that director Woliner thought helped discredit him; producers noted timing with review embargo lift amplified impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical production operational practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use operational safeguards like chemistry tests, staged cover stories (posing as a documentary crew), and careful choice of shoot methods to elicit genuine reactions while protecting the production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team staged a 'documentary crew' scenario for chemistry tests with an English couple; they flew promising actors for in-person tests and used cover stories to avoid detection.
